metadata.title: Bank & fintech digital-money consortia - exhaustive membership (stablecoin venture, Clearing House tokenized deposits, Zelle ZLUSD, JPM Kinexys, Open USD) + the CRE-pressured regional-bank fragility
metadata.frame: Who controls tokenized-dollar issuance. Four+ overlapping consortia: (1) a 21-firm USD STABLECOIN venture (Sep 1 2026); (2) The Clearing House shared TOKENIZED-DEPOSIT network (17 participants; deposits stay in-bank, FDIC-eligible - the defensive answer to the issuer-yield ban); (3) Zelle/Early Warning ZLUSD (7 bank owners); (4) JPMorgan Kinexys (solo, ~$7B/day - why JPM sat out #1); (5) fintech Open USD/Open Standard (140+; undercuts Circle/Tether). Every NAMED member is wired; Open USD's ~115+ unnamed partners are flagged, not silently completed.
metadata.grade: membership + launch facts = FACT (rosters from Sep-2026 reporting). 'Incumbents fixing the game to keep issuance theirs' = LABELED interpretation. Per-bank CRE ratios = to verify from FDIC call reports.
metadata.cre_fragility: The acute risk sits with CRE-concentrated regional banks (Regions/Fifth Third/KeyBank/Huntington/Citizens/Truist appear across these networks): ~5x more CRE-exposed than big banks; CRE >50% of loans at <$10B banks; $1.5-2T CRE maturities 2024-26; most core-deposit-reliant. A stablecoin/affiliate-yield deposit drain would squeeze exactly these banks as the maturity wall bites - 'can't weather a mild storm'. (Some - Regions/PNC/M&T/First Horizon/US Bancorp/KeyCorp - are RE-ENTERING CRE in 2026, adding risk.)
metadata.japan_bond_caveat: The yen/JGB carry-trade channel (macro-carry-trades) runs mainly through LARGE institutions' FX/rates books, not community-bank balance sheets - so it is a separate large-institution fragility, not the small-bank CRE channel (per the corpus; flagged, not asserted as a small-bank link).
metadata.honest_correction: The ABA does NOT organize a stablecoin consortium; it LOBBIES to close the yield loophole in the name of community banks - a position that also benefits large banks. Whether that = ordinary trade-association alignment or large-bank 'pressure/capture' is graded, not asserted.

Open USD (OUSD): fintech/card-network/asset-manager consortium stablecoin - shared economics undercut Circle/Tether (Circle -15-17% on announce). Notably ABSENT: Tether, Circle, PayPal. ~115+ further partners unnamed here (NOT silently complete) (fact).

Regions_Financial: regional bank in these consortia that is also CRE-concentrated. Community/regional banks are ~5x more CRE-exposed than big banks; CRE often >50% of loans under $10B assets; $1.5-2T CRE maturity wall 2024-26; 300%-of-capital = supervisory flag (fact; per-bank ratio to verify).

The intersection that matters: the banks most CRE-concentrated + most core-deposit-reliant are the ones a stablecoin/yield deposit-drain would squeeze precisely as the CRE maturity wall bites - i.e., least able to weather a mild storm (BRG/Fed/CRS) (fact of exposure; timing/severity graded).

American Bankers Association (via its Community Bankers Council) lobbies to CLOSE the yield loophole (extend the interest ban to affiliates/partners), warning up to $6.6T deposits at risk. NOTE: ABA is NOT running a stablecoin consortium - it opposes yield-bearing stablecoins in the NAME of community banks, a posture that also serves large banks (fact of advocacy; 'captured/pressured' read graded).
